items.title: Lego Unveils Daft Punk Set Based on 2007 ‘Alive’ Tour, Short Film Collab Set to ‘Human After All’
items.summary:
Lego and Daft Punk have entered into a collaboration that covers products, short-form content and brand experiences, built around a fan-designed set modeled on the pyramid stage from the duo's 2007 "Alive" tour. The design came through Lego Ideas, the company's crowdsourcing platform, where users submit concepts and gather public support.

The "Daft Punk Concert" project came from a father-and-son team in Belgium, who first entered it in a music-themed Lego Ideas competition in 2020 and won the grand prize. Variety reported that the submission has since cleared 10,000 supporters on the platform, the threshold that moves a design into the next stage of development.

Daft Punk creative director Cédric Hervet framed the choice of subject as a nod to the people who built the design. "The pyramid stage is one of the most recognisable expressions of Daft Punk's visual world, so it feels fitting that this fan-created design will be centre stage of this partnership," he said. "Fans have always played an important part in Daft Punk's story, and we are excited to see that creativity reflected through the Lego universe."

To launch the partnership, the two sides made a 48-second film in which the duo appear as Minifigures, helmets included, trailing a holographic red brick across a desert. The soundtrack draws on a bassline from 2001's "Discovery" and the title track from 2005's "Human After All."

Lego's chief product and marketing officer, Julia Goldin, pointed to the shared audience. "Like the Lego brand, Daft Punk inspires generations through creativity, innovation and a deep connection with fans," she said, calling the collaboration "just the beginning of a bigger journey." The company's announcement promises further events and content across music and culture without specifying what or when.

The duo have appeared in brick form before, turning up as Minifigures in Pharrell Williams' 2024 Lego-animated documentary "Piece by Piece"; Williams and Nile Rodgers worked with them on "Get Lucky." For now, the pyramid set remains in development at Lego Ideas, with no release date announced.

items.title: ‘SNL’ Sets John Mulaney’s Seventh Time Hosting With Phoebe Bridgers as Musical Guest, Plus Druski and the Strokes
items.summary:
NBC has filled out the November lineup for "Saturday Night Live," with John Mulaney hosting the Nov. 14 episode alongside musical guest Phoebe Bridgers, and Druski headlining Nov. 7 with the Strokes. The announcements extend a Season 52 slate that has leaned on athletes, comedians and first-timers.

Mulaney's booking marks his seventh time hosting, which puts him among the show's most frequent hosts, though well short of Alec Baldwin's record 17 stints. He wrote for the show for four seasons between 2008 and 2012. He appears in the upcoming Amazon Prime Video film "Madden" and is currently touring stand-up under the banner "Mister Whatever."

Bridgers will make her third appearance as musical guest, following her 2021 debut and a return with her Boygenius bandmates Lucy Dacus and Julien Baker. She is on the road behind her recent album "Lost Weekend."

Druski's episode makes him the first digital content creator to headline the sketch series, as Variety reported, and it lands ahead of the December premiere of his scripted Netflix series "Collect and Praise." The Strokes will back him as musical guest for their fifth time on the show, currently touring in support of "Reality Awaits."

Before those two, the Halloween episode goes to "Obsession" star Inde Navarette with Gracie Abrams. Season 52 opened Sept. 26 with New York Knicks guard Jalen Brunson hosting and Katseye performing, followed by Dakota Johnson with Turnstile and a Taylor Swift cameo, then Shane Gillis on Oct. 10, whose monologue joke about how women dress at the gym drew immediate criticism.

items.title: Christina Aguilera Joins Chappell Roan for “Coffee” at Super Graphic Spectacular in LA: Watch
items.summary:
Christina Aguilera turned up unannounced at the Shrine in Los Angeles on Wednesday, October 21st, joining Chappell Roan during the first night of Roan's Super Graphic Spectacular benefit concert. Aguilera performed "Beautiful" on her own before singing "Coffee" as a duet with Roan.

Roan introduced her guest with a short speech crediting Aguilera with clearing ground for the pop singers who followed. "She paved the way for me and all women in pop to do whatever the fuck they want and sing and wear whatever the fuck they want," Roan told the crowd. "And she definitely walks so I can fucking run."

Aguilera returned the compliment before her set. "From the moment I heard Chappell's voice, I knew she was a force to be reckoned with, and I became an immediate fan," she said, going on to tell the audience that feeling insecure or lost is common and that "you can never let anybody bring you down." She then played a piano-led "Beautiful" while Roan sat and watched.

The two split "Coffee," a ballad from Roan's 2023 debut "The Rise and Fall of a Midwestern Princess," with Roan taking the first verse and Aguilera the second before they harmonized through the bridge and final chorus. According to Consequence, Roan appeared visibly nervous at the start and settled quickly, and Aguilera told her afterward that she loves the song. Fan-shot video of the performance circulated after the show.

Tinashe and Lola Young also performed on Wednesday's bill. The second night, on October 22nd, features Caroline Polachek, MUNA and another set from Roan. Proceeds from the two-night event go to trans youth and LGBTQ+ organizations through Roan's Midwest Princess Project.
